Jay R. McDaniel

Attorney · CVA · CEPA · Partner, Scarinci Hollenbeck

Jay McDaniel is special valuation counsel to owners of closely held businesses. He is a lawyer who is also a Certified Valuation Analyst and a Certified Exit Planning Advisor, and his practice sits where those three disciplines meet: the valuation of a private business, the disputes that break out over who owns it and what it is worth, and the transitions that end a period of ownership. Owners hire him to protect, enhance, and realize the value of what they have built — through litigation when it comes to that, and through planning when it does not.

Much of the work is business divorce. When the owners of a closely held company decide they can no longer own it together, the fight is about control and about the number, and Jay has spent three decades on both sides of it — representing majorities and minorities in oppression claims, deadlock, breach of fiduciary duty, and forced buyouts. The valuation background is what he brings to those cases that most litigators cannot: the worth of the business, or of an owner's stake in it, is usually the thing the case is actually about, and he argues it with the standards and methods a court will credit.

Beyond the courtroom, he advises family-owned, founder-led, and investor-backed companies on governance, management transitions, partner exits, and the operating-agreement engineering that prevents disputes before they start. His commercial and intellectual-property litigation practice — restrictive covenants, trade secrets, unfair competition, trademarks, and copyrights — rounds out the work, usually in disputes over confidential information, employee mobility, and contract enforcement.

Credentials

Certified Valuation Analyst (CVA), National Association of Certified Valuators and Analysts. Certified Exit Planning Advisor (CEPA), Exit Planning Institute. J.D., Rutgers Law School, Order of the Coif. B.A., Rutgers University.

Admissions

Admitted in New York and New Jersey. Admitted before the U.S. District Courts for the District of New Jersey and the Eastern, Southern, and Northern Districts of New York; the U.S. Courts of Appeals for the Second and Third Circuits; and the Supreme Court of the United States.

Selected matters

His reported decisions include Brownstein v. Lindsay, 742 F.3d 55 (3d Cir. 2014), a landmark ruling that federal courts lack authority to cancel copyright registrations, which arose from a business divorce over software co-authorship; Delaney v. Dykstra (N.J. App. Div. 2019), an LLC-member oppression matter; and a decade of litigation in Anello Fence, LLC v. VCA Sons, Inc. in the District of New Jersey and the Third Circuit. Most closely held business disputes resolve through confidential settlement, non-public arbitration, or unpublished bench rulings; additional matters are available on request.

Writing and speaking

Jay is the editor and principal author of the Business Divorce Law Report and produces short video breakdowns on the @CloselyHeld channel. He lectures frequently on business valuation, partner disputes, governance, and the dynamics of closely held companies, including recent programs for NJICLE, Strafford, and BARBRI.
